title: How Was Your Day Yesterday? | Past Simple English Conversation Practice | A2–B1

segments.text: Hello everyone and welcome back to Mr.
segments.ipa: /həˈloʊ ˈɛvriˌwʌn ənd ˈwɛlkəm bæk tu ˈmɪstər/

segments.text: English Channel where learning English is easy and fun. I'm Emily. Hello Emily. Hi everyone.
segments.ipa: /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl wɛr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ˈizi ənd fʌn aɪm ˈɛmɪli həˈloʊ ˈɛmɪli haɪ ˈɛvriˌwʌn/

segments.text: I'm Paul and I'm happy you're here.
segments.ipa: /aɪm pɔl ənd aɪm ˈhæpi jʊr hir/

segments.text: Emily, how was your day yesterday?
segments.ipa: /ˈɛmɪli haʊ wɑz jɔr deɪ ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ/

segments.text: It was pretty good, thanks.
segments.ipa: /ɪt wɑz ˈprɪti ɡʊd θæŋks/

segments.text: My morning was a little busy, but I had a nice lunch with my sister.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈmɔrnɪŋ wɑz ə ˈlɪtəl ˈbɪzi bʌt aɪ hæd ə naɪs lʌntʃ wɪð maɪ ˈsɪstər/

segments.text: How about you?

segments.text: Mine was okay.
segments.ipa: /maɪn wɑz ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: Nothing special happened, but I felt tired by the evening.
segments.ipa: /ˈnʌθɪŋ ˈspɛʃəl ˈhæpənd bʌt aɪ fɛlt ˈtaɪərd baɪ ðə ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: Actually, I almost answered your question with just fine.
segments.ipa: /ˈækˌtʃuəli aɪ ˈɔlˌmoʊst ˈænsərd jɔr ˈkwɛstʃən wɪð dʒʌst faɪn/

segments.text: That's such a common answer.
segments.ipa: /ðæts sʌtʃ ə ˈkɑmən ˈænsər/

segments.text: Fine works, but sometimes I don't know what to ask next when someone gives me only that word, right?
segments.ipa: /faɪn wɝks bʌt səmˈtaɪmz aɪ doʊnt noʊ wʌt tu æsk nɛkst wɛn ˈsʌmˌwʌn ɡɪvz mi ˈoʊnli ðæt wɝd raɪt/

segments.text: Although sometimes fine means exactly that.
segments.ipa: /ˌɔlˈðoʊ səmˈtaɪmz faɪn minz ɪɡˈzæktli ðæt/

segments.text: My day wasn't amazing and it wasn't terrible.
segments.ipa: /maɪ deɪ ˈwɑzənt əˈmeɪzɪŋ ənd ɪt ˈwɑzənt ˈtɛrəbəl/

segments.text: Do I really need an interesting story? No.
segments.ipa: /du aɪ ˈrɪli nid æn ˈɪntrəstɪŋ ˈstɔri noʊ/

segments.text: An ordinary detail is enough.
segments.ipa: /æn ˈɔrdəˌnɛri dɪˈteɪl ɪz ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: You could say it was fine.
segments.ipa: /ju kʊd seɪ ɪt wɑz faɪn/

segments.text: I made breakfast and went for a walk.
segments.ipa: /aɪ meɪd ˈbrɛkfəst ənd wɛnt fɔr ə wɔk/

segments.text: That gives me something to ask about. Oh, okay.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɡɪvz mi ˈsʌmθɪŋ tu æsk əˈbaʊt oʊ ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: Then here's my real answer.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn hɪrz maɪ ril ˈænsər/

segments.text: It was okay.
segments.ipa: /ɪt wɑz ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: I woke up early, but I stayed in bed too long.
segments.ipa: /aɪ woʊk ʌp ˈɝli bʌt aɪ steɪd ɪn bɛd tu lɔŋ/

segments.text: There's your exciting story.
segments.ipa: /ðɛrz jɔr ɪkˈsaɪtɪŋ ˈstɔri/

segments.text: Now, I'm curious.
segments.ipa: /naʊ aɪm ˈkjʊriəs/

segments.text: Were you resting or were you looking at your phone?
segments.ipa: /wɝ ju ˈrɛstɪŋ ɔr wɝ ju ˈlʊkɪŋ æt jɔr foʊn/

segments.text: Looking at my phone.
segments.ipa: /ˈlʊkɪŋ æt maɪ foʊn/

segments.text: I checked the weather and somehow that became 20 minutes of watching someone make a sandwich.
segments.ipa: /aɪ tʃɛkt ðə ˈwɛðər ənd ˈsʌmˌhaʊ ðæt bɪˈkeɪm ˈmɪnəts ʌv ˈwɑtʃɪŋ ˈsʌmˌwʌn meɪk ə ˈsændwɪtʃ/

segments.text: A sandwich before breakfast?
segments.ipa: /ə ˈsændwɪtʃ bɪˈfɔr ˈbrɛkfəst/

segments.text: That sounds dangerous.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz ˈdeɪndʒərəs/

segments.text: Did it at least give you an idea for something to eat?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ɪt æt list ɡɪv ju æn aɪˈdiə fɔr ˈsʌmθɪŋ tu it/

segments.text: It did, but I didn't have the ingredients.
segments.ipa: /ɪt dɪd bʌt aɪ ˈdɪdənt hæv ðə ˌɪnˈɡridiənts/

segments.text: So, my yesterday started with big sandwich dreams and a very small bowl of cereal.
segments.ipa: /soʊ maɪ ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ ˈstɑrtɪd wɪð bɪɡ ˈsændwɪtʃ drimz ənd ə ˈvɛri smɔl boʊl ʌv ˈsɪriəl/

segments.text: See, that's a perfectly good answer to how was your day yesterday.
segments.ipa: /si ðæts ə ˈpɝfəktli ɡʊd ˈænsər tu haʊ wɑz jɔr deɪ ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ/

segments.text: You don't need a trip or a big event.
segments.ipa: /ju doʊnt nid ə trɪp ɔr ə bɪɡ ɪˈvɛnt/

segments.text: Small details can be fun.
segments.ipa: /smɔl dɪˈteɪlz kæn bi fʌn/

segments.text: That helps because I think learners sometimes feel pressure to give a wonderful answer.
segments.ipa: /ðæt hɛlps bɪˈkɔz aɪ θɪŋk ˈlɝnərz səmˈtaɪmz fil ˈprɛʃər tu ɡɪv ə ˈwʌndərfəl ˈænsər/

segments.text: Can they just say, "Pretty good, thanks.
segments.ipa: /kæn ðeɪ dʒʌst seɪ ˈprɪti ɡʊd θæŋks/

segments.text: How about you?" Absolutely.
segments.ipa: /haʊ əˈbaʊt ju ˌæbsəˈlutli/

segments.text: That's friendly and natural, especially when you don't have much time.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈfrɛndli ənd ˈnætʃərəl əˈspɛʃli wɛn ju doʊnt hæv mʌtʃ taɪm/

segments.text: You answer the question and give the other person a chance to speak.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈænsər ðə ˈkwɛstʃən ənd ɡɪv ðə ˈʌðər ˈpɝsən ə tʃæns tu spik/

segments.text: What if the day was difficult?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf ðə deɪ wɑz ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: Sometimes pretty good feels wrong, but I don't want to explain every problem before someone's had their coffee.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ˈprɪti ɡʊd filz rɔŋ bʌt aɪ doʊnt wɑnt tu ɪkˈspleɪn ˈɛvəri ˈprɑbləm bɪˈfɔr ˈsʌmˌwʌnz hæd ðɛr ˈkɑfi/

segments.text: You could say, "It was a little tiring, but I'm okay.
segments.ipa: /ju kʊd seɪ ɪt wɑz ə ˈlɪtəl ˈtaɪrɪŋ bʌt aɪm ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: You're being honest, and you can choose whether to say more."
segments.ipa: /jʊr ˈbiɪŋ ˈɑnəst ənd ju kæn tʃuz ˈwɛðər tu seɪ mɔr/

segments.text: I like that.
segments.ipa: /aɪ laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: A little tiring describes the day, but I'd say I was tired when I'm talking about myself, right? Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈlɪtəl ˈtaɪrɪŋ dɪˈskraɪbz ðə deɪ bʌt aɪd seɪ aɪ wɑz ˈtaɪərd wɛn aɪm ˈtɔkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ˌmaɪˈsɛlf raɪt ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: Yesterday was tiring, so you were tired.
segments.ipa: /ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ wɑz ˈtaɪrɪŋ soʊ ju wɝ ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: For example, my morning was busy and I was tired after breakfast.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl maɪ ˈmɔrnɪŋ wɑz ˈbɪzi ənd aɪ wɑz ˈtaɪərd ˈæftər ˈbrɛkfəst/

segments.text: After breakfast already?
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈbrɛkfəst ɔlˈrɛdi/

segments.text: That sounds like a difficult start.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz laɪk ə ˈdɪfəkəlt stɑrt/

segments.text: Was your morning yesterday really that busy?
segments.ipa: /wɑz jɔr ˈmɔrnɪŋ ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ ˈrɪli ðæt ˈbɪzi/

segments.text: Well, I woke up at 6:30 because I wanted a quiet morning.
segments.ipa: /wɛl aɪ woʊk ʌp æt bɪˈkɔz aɪ ˈwɔntɪd ə ˈkwaɪət ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: I planned to have coffee before doing anything else.
segments.ipa: /aɪ plænd tu hæv ˈkɑfi bɪˈfɔr ˈduɪŋ ˈɛniˌθɪŋ ɛls/

segments.text: 6:30 sounds peaceful in theory.
segments.ipa: /saʊndz ˈpisfəl ɪn ˈθɪri/

segments.text: Did you actually get up then or did you stay under the blanket for a while?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju ˈækˌtʃuəli ɡɛt ʌp ðɛn ɔr dɪd ju steɪ ˈʌndər ðə ˈblæŋkət fɔr ə waɪl/

segments.text: I got up right away surprisingly.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ɡɑt ʌp raɪt əˈweɪ sərˈpraɪzɪŋli/

segments.text: And there's a useful difference.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðɛrz ə ˈjusfəl ˈdɪfərəns/

segments.text: I woke up when my alarm rang then I got up and left my bed.
segments.ipa: /aɪ woʊk ʌp wɛn maɪ əˈlɑrm ræŋ ðɛn aɪ ɡɑt ʌp ənd lɛft maɪ bɛd/

segments.text: Ah, so yesterday I woke up at 7, but I got up at 7:20.
segments.ipa: /ɑ soʊ ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ aɪ woʊk ʌp æt bʌt aɪ ɡɑt ʌp æt/

segments.text: My body needed a second invitation, apparently.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈbɑdi ˈnidəd ə ˈsɛkənd ˌɪnvɪˈteɪʃən əˈpɛrəntli/

segments.text: Did you set another alarm or did you suddenly notice the time?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju sɛt əˈnʌðər əˈlɑrm ɔr dɪd ju ˈsʌdənli ˈnoʊtəs ðə taɪm/

segments.text: I noticed the time on my phone.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈnoʊtəst ðə taɪm ɑn maɪ foʊn/

segments.text: Then I thought, "Oh no."
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ θɔt oʊ noʊ/

segments.text: Put it down and went straight to the kitchen.
segments.ipa: /pʊt ɪt daʊn ənd wɛnt streɪt tu ðə ˈkɪtʃən/

segments.text: That sounds familiar.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz fəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: I went to the kitchen, too, but I found an empty coffee bag.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɛnt tu ðə ˈkɪtʃən tu bʌt aɪ faʊnd æn ˈɛmpti ˈkɑfi bæɡ/

segments.text: My quiet morning suddenly needed a new plan.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈkwaɪət ˈmɔrnɪŋ ˈsʌdənli ˈnidəd ə nu plæn/

segments.text: Oh, that's disappointing.
segments.ipa: /oʊ ðæts ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪŋ/

segments.text: Did you make tea instead or leave the house to buy coffee?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju meɪk ti ˌɪnˈstɛd ɔr liv ðə haʊs tu baɪ ˈkɑfi/

segments.text: I made tea.
segments.ipa: /aɪ meɪd ti/

segments.text: I didn't want to get dressed just to buy a drink.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈdɪdənt wɑnt tu ɡɛt drɛst dʒʌst tu baɪ ə drɪŋk/

segments.text: Then I had toast and a banana for breakfast.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ hæd toʊst ənd ə bəˈnænə fɔr ˈbrɛkfəst/

segments.text: You said I had toast.
segments.ipa: /ju sɛd aɪ hæd toʊst/

segments.text: That's useful because had can describe food and drinks.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈjusfəl bɪˈkɔz hæd kæn dɪˈskraɪb fud ənd drɪŋks/

segments.text: I had cereal and you had tea. Yep.
segments.ipa: /aɪ hæd ˈsɪriəl ənd ju hæd ti jɛp/

segments.text: You can also say I ate toast or I drank tea.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈɔlsoʊ seɪ aɪ eɪt toʊst ɔr aɪ dræŋk ti/

segments.text: But I had breakfast is a simple way to talk about the meal.
segments.ipa: /bʌt aɪ hæd ˈbrɛkfəst ɪz ə ˈsɪmpəl weɪ tu tɔk əˈbaʊt ðə mil/

segments.text: And if someone asks what I had, I can add the details.
segments.ipa: /ənd ɪf ˈsʌmˌwʌn æsks wʌt aɪ hæd aɪ kæn æd ðə dɪˈteɪlz/

segments.text: Yesterday I had cereal with milk and I ate it standing beside the sink. Standing up.
segments.ipa: /ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ aɪ hæd ˈsɪriəl wɪð mɪlk ənd aɪ eɪt ɪt ˈstændɪŋ bɪˈsaɪd ðə sɪŋk ˈstændɪŋ ʌp/

segments.text: Were you in a hurry or was every chair covered with clothes?
segments.ipa: /wɝ ju ɪn ə ˈhɝi ɔr wɑz ˈɛvəri tʃɛr ˈkʌvərd wɪð kloʊðz/

segments.text: Just in a hurry.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst ɪn ə ˈhɝi/

segments.text: The chairs were innocent.
segments.ipa: /ðə tʃɛrz wɝ ˈɪnəsənt/

segments.text: I needed to get ready and I couldn't find the shirt I wanted.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈnidəd tu ɡɛt ˈrɛdi ənd aɪ ˈkʊdənt faɪnd ðə ʃɝt aɪ ˈwɔntɪd/

segments.text: What did you wear instead?
segments.ipa: /wʌt dɪd ju wɛr ˌɪnˈstɛd/

segments.text: Please tell me you didn't spend another 20 minutes choosing. Thankfully, no.
segments.ipa: /pliz tɛl mi ju ˈdɪdənt spɛnd əˈnʌðər ˈmɪnəts ˈtʃuzɪŋ ˈθæŋkfəli noʊ/

segments.text: I wore a blue shirt that was right in front of me.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɔr ə blu ʃɝt ðæt wɑz raɪt ɪn frʌnt ʌv mi/

segments.text: Then I brushed my teeth and looked for my keys.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ brʌʃt maɪ tiθ ənd lʊkt fɔr maɪ kiz/

segments.text: Let me guess, they were in your pocket.
segments.ipa: /lɛt mi ɡɛs ðeɪ wɝ ɪn jɔr ˈpɑkət/

segments.text: That's where mine usually are when I say I can't find them.
segments.ipa: /ðæts wɛr maɪn ˈjuʒəwəli ɑr wɛn aɪ seɪ aɪ kænt faɪnd ðɛm/

segments.text: They were beside the door, actually.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɝ bɪˈsaɪd ðə dɔr ˈækˌtʃuəli/

segments.text: I walked past them twice.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɔkt pæst ðɛm twaɪs/

segments.text: What time did you leave home yesterday?
segments.ipa: /wʌt taɪm dɪd ju liv hoʊm ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ/

segments.text: I left at 8:15.
segments.ipa: /aɪ lɛft æt/

segments.text: Before that, I took a shower, got dressed, and packed my bag.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈfɔr ðæt aɪ tʊk ə ˈʃaʊər ɡɑt drɛst ənd pækt maɪ bæɡ/

segments.text: I also filled my water bottle.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈɔlsoʊ fɪld maɪ ˈwɔtər ˈbɑtəl/

segments.text: That sounds organized.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz ˈɔrɡəˌnaɪzd/

segments.text: When you describe it, those little words help.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju dɪˈskraɪb ɪt ðoʊz ˈlɪtəl wɝdz hɛlp/

segments.text: Before that, then, and also I can follow your morning easily.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈfɔr ðæt ðɛn ənd ˈɔlsoʊ aɪ kæn ˈfɑloʊ jɔr ˈmɔrnɪŋ ˈizəli/

segments.text: They help me remember it, too.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ hɛlp mi rɪˈmɛmbər ɪt tu/

segments.text: But you don't need every step.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju doʊnt nid ˈɛvəri stɛp/

segments.text: What would your short version sound like?
segments.ipa: /wʌt wʊd jɔr ʃɔrt ˈvɝʒən saʊnd laɪk/

segments.text: Yesterday, I woke up at 7 and had cereal for breakfast.
segments.ipa: /ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ aɪ woʊk ʌp æt ənd hæd ˈsɪriəl fɔr ˈbrɛkfəst/

segments.text: Then I got dressed and left home.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ ɡɑt drɛst ənd lɛft hoʊm/

segments.text: Should I mention the phone?
segments.ipa: /ʃʊd aɪ ˈmɛnʃən ðə foʊn/

segments.text: Only if you want to explain why you hurried.
segments.ipa: /ˈoʊnli ɪf ju wɑnt tu ɪkˈspleɪn waɪ ju ˈhɝid/

segments.text: You could add, "I spent too much time on my phone, so I got ready quickly."

segments.text: That's definitely the honest version.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ˈdɛfənətli ðə ˈɑnəst ˈvɝʒən/

segments.text: And once I finally stepped outside, I realized something else about my morning.
segments.ipa: /ənd wʌns aɪ ˈfaɪnəli stɛpt ˈaʊtˈsaɪd aɪ ˈriəˌlaɪzd ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɛls əˈbaʊt maɪ ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

segments.text: I hadn't checked what was in my bag.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈhædənt tʃɛkt wʌt wɑz ɪn maɪ bæɡ/

segments.text: Oh, what was missing?
segments.ipa: /oʊ wʌt wɑz ˈmɪsɪŋ/

segments.text: Please tell me you remembered your lunch after that tiny bowl of cereal.
segments.ipa: /pliz tɛl mi ju rɪˈmɛmbərd jɔr lʌntʃ ˈæftər ðæt ˈtaɪni boʊl ʌv ˈsɪriəl/

segments.text: My lunch was there, thankfully, but my notebook was on the kitchen table, and I needed it for a meeting. That's frustrating.
segments.ipa: /maɪ lʌntʃ wɑz ðɛr ˈθæŋkfəli bʌt maɪ ˈnoʊtˌbʊk wɑz ɑn ðə ˈkɪtʃən ˈteɪbəl ənd aɪ ˈnidəd ɪt fɔr ə ˈmitɪŋ ðæts ˈfrʌˌstreɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: Did you have time to go back or were you already too far from home?

segments.ipa: /aɪ laɪk ðæt ʃi æskt əˈbaʊt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju ˈmɛnʃənd/

segments.text: A good follow-up question often comes from a detail the other person gives you.
segments.ipa: /ə ɡʊd ˈfɑloʊˌʌp ˈkwɛstʃən ˈɔfən kʌmz frʌm ə dɪˈteɪl ðə ˈʌðər ˈpɝsən ɡɪvz ju/

segments.text: So if you say, "I had lunch with my sister."
segments.ipa: /soʊ ɪf ju seɪ aɪ hæd lʌntʃ wɪð maɪ ˈsɪstər/

segments.text: I could ask, "Does she live nearby?"
segments.ipa: /aɪ kʊd æsk dʌz ʃi laɪv ˈnɪrˈbaɪ/

segments.text: That feels more natural than changing the subject. Exactly.
segments.ipa: /ðæt filz mɔr ˈnætʃərəl ðæn ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ ðə səbˈdʒɛkt ɪɡˈzæktli/

segments.text: She lives about 20 minutes away.
segments.ipa: /ʃi lɪvz əˈbaʊt ˈmɪnəts əˈweɪ/

segments.text: Actually, we don't meet every week, so yesterday's lunch was a nice surprise.
segments.ipa: /ˈækˌtʃuəli wi doʊnt mit ˈɛvəri wik soʊ ˈjɛstərˌdeɪz lʌntʃ wɑz ə naɪs sərˈpraɪz/

segments.text: That makes me want to ask when you last saw her.
segments.ipa: /ðæt meɪks mi wɑnt tu æsk wɛn ju læst sɔ hɝ/

segments.text: But how many questions are too many?
segments.ipa: /bʌt haʊ ˈmɛni ˈkwɛstʃənz ɑr tu ˈmɛni/

segments.text: I don't want lunch to become an interview.
segments.ipa: /aɪ doʊnt wɑnt lʌntʃ tu bɪˈkʌm æn ˈɪntərvˌju/

segments.text: Give something back between questions.
segments.ipa: /ɡɪv ˈsʌmθɪŋ bæk bɪˈtwin ˈkwɛstʃənz/

segments.text: You could say, I haven't seen my brother this week.
segments.ipa: /ju kʊd seɪ aɪ ˈhævənt sin maɪ ˈbrʌðər ðɪs wik/

segments.text: Maybe I'll call him.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi aɪl kɔl hɪm/

segments.text: Then we're both sharing.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn wir boʊθ ˈʃɛrɪŋ/

segments.text: Ah, so I'm not just collecting information.
segments.ipa: /ɑ soʊ aɪm nɑt dʒʌst kəˈlɛktɪŋ ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/

segments.text: I'm letting your story remind me of something from my own life. Right?
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈlɛtɪŋ jɔr ˈstɔri riˈmaɪnd mi ʌv ˈsʌmθɪŋ frʌm maɪ oʊn laɪf raɪt/

segments.text: As long as you leave room for my story, too.
segments.ipa: /æz lɔŋ æz ju liv rum fɔr maɪ ˈstɔri tu/

segments.text: Have you ever answered a question and watched the other person immediately start talking about themselves? Definitely.
segments.ipa: /hæv ju ˈɛvər ˈænsərd ə ˈkwɛstʃən ənd wɑtʃt ðə ˈʌðər ˈpɝsən ˌɪˈmiˌdiətli stɑrt ˈtɔkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðɛmˈsɛlvz ˈdɛfənətli/

segments.text: I've probably done it myself when I got excited.
segments.ipa: /aɪv ˈprɑbəˌbli dʌn ɪt ˌmaɪˈsɛlf wɛn aɪ ɡɑt ɪkˈsaɪtəd/

segments.text: Sometimes I need to slow down and say, "Sorry, what happened next?"
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz aɪ nid tu sloʊ daʊn ənd seɪ ˈsɑri wʌt ˈhæpənd nɛkst/

segments.text: That little question can help.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ˈlɪtəl ˈkwɛstʃən kæn hɛlp/

segments.text: Another useful one is, "How did you feel about that?"
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˈjusfəl wʌn ɪz haʊ dɪd ju fil əˈbaʊt ðæt/

segments.text: But I'd save it for something that seems important. Fair.
segments.ipa: /bʌt aɪd seɪv ɪt fɔr ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt simz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt fɛr/

segments.text: If I bought toothpaste yesterday, you probably don't need to ask about my feelings.
segments.ipa: /ɪf aɪ bɑt ˈtuθˌpeɪst ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ ju ˈprɑbəˌbli doʊnt nid tu æsk əˈbaʊt maɪ ˈfilɪŋz/

segments.text: What about a short practice conversation?
segments.ipa: /wʌt əˈbaʊt ə ʃɔrt ˈpræktəs ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən/

segments.text: Let's try it.
segments.ipa: /lɛts traɪ ɪt/

segments.text: I'll tell you something ordinary.
segments.ipa: /aɪl tɛl ju ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈɔrdəˌnɛri/

segments.text: Yesterday evening, I cooked dinner at home. Nice.
segments.ipa: /ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ ˈivnɪŋ aɪ kʊkt ˈdɪnər æt hoʊm naɪs/

segments.text: What did you make?
segments.ipa: /wʌt dɪd ju meɪk/

segments.text: I'm asking because you mentioned cooking and because I'm always interested in dinner.
segments.ipa: /aɪm ˈæskɪŋ bɪˈkɔz ju ˈmɛnʃənd ˈkʊkɪŋ ənd bɪˈkɔz aɪm ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈɪntrəstɪd ɪn ˈdɪnər/

segments.text: I made rice with vegetables, but I cooked too much.
segments.ipa: /aɪ meɪd raɪs wɪð ˈvɛdʒtəbəlz bʌt aɪ kʊkt tu mʌtʃ/

segments.text: Now, you've got a few different things you could ask about.
segments.ipa: /naʊ juv ɡɑt ə fju ˈdɪfərənt θɪŋz ju kʊd æsk əˈbaʊt/

segments.text: I might share first.
segments.ipa: /aɪ maɪt ʃɛr fɝst/

segments.text: I always make too much rice, too.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈɔlˌweɪz meɪk tu mʌtʃ raɪs tu/

segments.text: Did you save some for today? Yep.
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju seɪv sʌm fɔr təˈdeɪ jɛp/

segments.text: I put some in the fridge.
segments.ipa: /aɪ pʊt sʌm ɪn ðə frɪdʒ/

segments.text: See how easily that moved forward?
segments.ipa: /si haʊ ˈizəli ðæt muvd ˈfɔrwərd/

segments.text: We didn't need a surprising story.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈdɪdənt nid ə sərˈpraɪzɪŋ ˈstɔri/

segments.text: And I learned something real about your evening.
segments.ipa: /ənd aɪ lɝnd ˈsʌmθɪŋ ril əˈbaʊt jɔr ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: Did you actually make rice yesterday or was that just our example?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju ˈækˌtʃuəli meɪk raɪs ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ ɔr wɑz ðæt dʒʌst ˈaʊər ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: I really did.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈrɪli dɪd/

segments.text: After dinner, I washed the dishes and listened to music.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈdɪnər aɪ wɑʃt ðə ˈdɪʃəz ənd ˈlɪsənd tu ˈmjuzɪk/

segments.text: Then I sat down with my book for a while.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn aɪ sæt daʊn wɪð maɪ bʊk fɔr ə waɪl/

segments.text: Did you enjoy having a quiet evening?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈhævɪŋ ə ˈkwaɪət ˈivnɪŋ/

segments.text: After errands and carrying bags, I'd probably want to stay on the couch.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər ˈɛrəndz ənd ˈkæriɪŋ bæɡz aɪd ˈprɑbəˌbli wɑnt tu steɪ ɑn ðə kaʊtʃ/

segments.text: I did, although I almost went out.
segments.ipa: /aɪ dɪd ˌɔlˈðoʊ aɪ ˈɔlˌmoʊst wɛnt aʊt/

segments.text: A friend invited me for a walk, but I didn't have much energy.
segments.ipa: /ə frɛnd ˌɪnˈvaɪtəd mi fɔr ə wɔk bʌt aɪ ˈdɪdənt hæv mʌtʃ ˈɛnərdʒi/

segments.text: Was it hard to say no?
segments.ipa: /wɑz ɪt hɑrd tu seɪ noʊ/

segments.text: Sometimes I agree to plans because I feel bad staying home a little.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz aɪ əˈɡri tu plænz bɪˈkɔz aɪ fil bæd ˈsteɪɪŋ hoʊm ə ˈlɪtəl/

segments.text: I said, "Thanks for asking, but I'm tired tonight.
segments.ipa: /aɪ sɛd θæŋks fɔr ˈæskɪŋ bʌt aɪm ˈtaɪərd təˈnaɪt/

segments.text: Could we walk tomorrow?"
segments.ipa: /kʊd wi wɔk təˈmɑˌroʊ/

segments.text: She was happy to choose another day.
segments.ipa: /ʃi wɑz ˈhæpi tu tʃuz əˈnʌðər deɪ/

segments.text: That sounds friendly.
segments.ipa: /ðæt saʊndz ˈfrɛndli/

segments.text: My evening was quiet, too.
segments.ipa: /maɪ ˈivnɪŋ wɑz ˈkwaɪət tu/

segments.text: After my neighbor picked up her package, I heated some soup and called my brother.
segments.ipa: /ˈæftər maɪ ˈneɪbər pɪkt ʌp hɝ ˈpækədʒ aɪ ˈhitəd sʌm sup ənd kɔld maɪ ˈbrʌðər/

segments.text: You mentioned wanting to call him earlier.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈmɛnʃənd ˈwɑntɪŋ tu kɔl hɪm ˈɝliər/

segments.text: So, you already had a chance yesterday.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ju ɔlˈrɛdi hæd ə tʃæns ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ/

segments.text: How's he doing? He's good.
segments.ipa: /haʊz hi ˈduɪŋ hiz ɡʊd/

segments.text: I was thinking about calling him again because we only talked briefly.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑz ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ˈkɔlɪŋ hɪm əˈɡɛn bɪˈkɔz wi ˈoʊnli tɔkt ˈbrifli/

segments.text: His daughter needed help with her homework.
segments.ipa: /hɪz ˈdɔtər ˈnidəd hɛlp wɪð hɝ ˈhoʊmˌwɝk/

segments.text: Oh, that explains it.
segments.ipa: /oʊ ðæt ɪkˈspleɪnz ɪt/

segments.text: Even a short call can be nice.
segments.ipa: /ˈivɪn ə ʃɔrt kɔl kæn bi naɪs/

segments.text: What did you do after you hung up?
segments.ipa: /wʌt dɪd ju du ˈæftər ju hʌŋ ʌp/

segments.text: I watched a cooking show.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑtʃt ə ˈkʊkɪŋ ʃoʊ/

segments.text: Apparently, yesterday began and ended with me watching other people make better food than mine.
segments.ipa: /əˈpɛrəntli ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ bɪˈɡæn ənd ˈɛndəd wɪð mi ˈwɑtʃɪŋ ˈʌðər ˈpipəl meɪk ˈbɛtər fud ðæn maɪn/

segments.text: Maybe tonight you'll cook something from the show.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi təˈnaɪt jul kʊk ˈsʌmθɪŋ frʌm ðə ʃoʊ/

segments.text: Did you stay up late watching it?
segments.ipa: /dɪd ju steɪ ʌp leɪt ˈwɑtʃɪŋ ɪt/

segments.text: No, I went to bed around 10:30.
segments.ipa: /noʊ aɪ wɛnt tu bɛd ərˈaʊnd/

segments.text: I put my phone across the room because I wanted an easier morning today.
segments.ipa: /aɪ pʊt maɪ foʊn əˈkrɔs ðə rum bɪˈkɔz aɪ ˈwɔntɪd æn ˈiziər ˈmɔrnɪŋ təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: That's a practical change after yesterday's slow start.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə ˈpræktəkəl tʃeɪndʒ ˈæftər ˈjɛstərˌdeɪz sloʊ stɑrt/

segments.text: If someone asked about your whole day now, what would you say?
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈsʌmˌwʌn æskt əˈbaʊt jɔr hoʊl deɪ naʊ wʌt wʊd ju seɪ/

segments.text: Yesterday was a little stressful at first.
segments.ipa: /ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ wɑz ə ˈlɪtəl ˈstrɛsfəl æt fɝst/

segments.text: I missed my bus, but work went okay.
segments.ipa: /aɪ mɪst maɪ bʌs bʌt wɝk wɛnt ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: In the evening, I had soup and talked to my brother.
segments.ipa: /ɪn ðə ˈivnɪŋ aɪ hæd sup ənd tɔkt tu maɪ ˈbrʌðər/

segments.text: That gives me a clear picture.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɡɪvz mi ə klɪr ˈpɪktʃər/

segments.text: You shared what happened, included a feeling, and chose a few details that mattered to you.
segments.ipa: /ju ʃɛrd wʌt ˈhæpənd ˌɪnˈkludəd ə ˈfilɪŋ ənd tʃoʊz ə fju dɪˈteɪlz ðæt ˈmætərd tu ju/

segments.text: What would your answer sound like?
segments.ipa: /wʌt wʊd jɔr ˈænsər saʊnd laɪk/

segments.text: Would the forgotten plants be the first thing you mentioned? Probably not.
segments.ipa: /wʊd ðə fərˈɡɑtən plænts bi ðə fɝst θɪŋ ju ˈmɛnʃənd ˈprɑbəˌbli nɑt/

segments.text: Yesterday was busy, but I enjoyed lunch with my sister.
segments.ipa: /ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ wɑz ˈbɪzi bʌt aɪ ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪd lʌntʃ wɪð maɪ ˈsɪstər/

segments.text: I ran some errands, then spent a quiet evening at home. Interesting.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ræn sʌm ˈɛrəndz ðɛn spɛnt ə ˈkwaɪət ˈivnɪŋ æt hoʊm ˈɪntrəstɪŋ/

segments.text: You didn't hide the difficult parts.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈdɪdənt haɪd ðə ˈdɪfəkəlt pɑrts/

segments.text: You just didn't let one forgotten task describe your whole day.
segments.ipa: /ju dʒʌst ˈdɪdənt lɛt wʌn fərˈɡɑtən tæsk dɪˈskraɪb jɔr hoʊl deɪ/

segments.text: Yes, because lunch mattered, too.
segments.ipa: /jɛs bɪˈkɔz lʌntʃ ˈmætərd tu/

segments.text: When I remember yesterday, I want to make room for my sister's laugh, not only my mistakes.
segments.ipa: /wɛn aɪ rɪˈmɛmbər ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ aɪ wɑnt tu meɪk rum fɔr maɪ ˈsɪstərz læf nɑt ˈoʊnli maɪ mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: I can do that with the mist bus.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn du ðæt wɪð ðə mɪst bʌs/

segments.text: It happened, but so did helping my coworker and hearing my brother's voice.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈhæpənd bʌt soʊ dɪd ˈhɛlpɪŋ maɪ ˈkoʊˈwɝkər ənd ˈhirɪŋ maɪ ˈbrʌðərz vɔɪs/

segments.text: And when you talk about your own yesterday, your English doesn't have to be perfect.
segments.ipa: /ənd wɛn ju tɔk əˈbaʊt jɔr oʊn ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈdʌzənt hæv tu bi pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: A few honest words can help someone know you better.
segments.ipa: /ə fju ˈɑnəst wɝdz kæn hɛlp ˈsʌmˌwʌn noʊ ju ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: You can pause, choose a simple verb, and try again.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn pɔz tʃuz ə ˈsɪmpəl vɝb ənd traɪ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: I went, I had, or I felt can be enough to begin.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɛnt aɪ hæd ɔr aɪ fɛlt kæn bi ɪˈnʌf tu bɪˈɡɪn/

segments.text: Thanks for spending this time with us on Mr.
segments.ipa: /θæŋks fɔr ˈspɛndɪŋ ðɪs taɪm wɪð ʌs ɑn ˈmɪstər/

segments.text: English Channel, where learning English is easy and fun.
segments.ipa: /ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈtʃænəl wɛr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ˈizi ənd fʌn/

segments.text: Keep practicing and be kind to yourself.
segments.ipa: /kip ˈpræktəsɪŋ ənd bi kaɪnd tu jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: We'll see you next time, everyone.
segments.ipa: /wil si ju nɛkst taɪm ˈɛvriˌwʌn/

segments.text: Take care and goodbye from both of us.
segments.ipa: /teɪk kɛr ənd ˌɡʊdˈbaɪ frʌm boʊθ ʌv ʌs/
